g1-implement.title: open — the lifecycle module and open_work: implement
g1-implement.imperative:
Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md for g1 and dispatch a constellation-implementer crew through scripts/run_crew.py with --parent naming THIS Commander session (never the Admiral) and an explicit --model sonnet. TASK: Build scripts/spine_lifecycle.py per LIFECYCLE_CONTRACT.md sections 2 and 3: the pure helpers (worktree_path_for, branch_name_for, archive_name_for, build_origin, closeout_refusal) and the impure open_work. open_work derives branch and worktree from work_id, refuses an occupied path AND a work id whose spine carries an engine_session with status 'active' (the ONLY two statuses checklist_engine ever writes are 'active' and 'released' -- there is no 'abandoned' engine_session; that field belongs to crew-runs.json, not here), provisions with git worktree add, scaffolds via init_work_area, compiles via generate_spine (imported, never re-implemented), injects the top-level origin block and re-validates, then self-verifies with verify_worktree_isolation.check_distinct_real in-process rather than trusting git's exit code. Any failure at or after the worktree add rolls back the worktree AND the branch this call created, scoped to what this call created, and refuses legibly. No door wiring in this gate. Regenerate the code map (python -m scripts.code_map build) because this gate adds a module; never hand-edit map/INDEX.md.

CLOSE CRITERIA:
- open_work refuses an occupied worktree path, and refuses a work id whose spine carries an active non-abandoned engine_session -- both by name, both with a VIOLATING fixture
- a late failure after git worktree add leaves NO worktree and NO branch behind (rollback proven against git worktree list --porcelain, not against an assertion string)
- check_distinct_real returning not-ok forces a rollback even when git worktree add exited 0
- the origin block survives a real claim/start/attest/advance drive byte-identical
- the pure helpers take today/wt_root as parameters so no test needs to freeze a clock or a host path
- open_work writes the spine as spine.json and LIFECYCLE_CONTRACT.md section 3 says so; close_work must never assume that name (see g2)

Every guard needs a VIOLATING case and an INNOCENT case in the tests/test_mcp_adoption.py::_cli_only_verb_violations house style -- a test that exercises only the happy path measures the mechanism, not the boundary. Attach the returned IMPLEMENTER_RESULT with --field status=complete.

g2-implement.title: close — archive, commit, and say it is ready: implement
g2-implement.imperative:
Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md for g2 and dispatch a constellation-implementer crew through scripts/run_crew.py with --parent naming THIS Commander session (never the Admiral) and an explicit --model sonnet. TASK: Add closeout_refusal (pure) and close_work (impure) to scripts/spine_lifecycle.py per LIFECYCLE_CONTRACT.md section 4. close_work refuses doing NOTHING AT ALL unless the lease is released, every item is terminal (computed from the spine dict INSIDE the pure closeout_refusal -- do NOT call run_crew.spine_terminal from it: that function takes a PATH and reads the file, so a pure dict-in predicate cannot call it. Instead ship a DIFFERENTIAL test asserting closeout_refusal's terminality verdict agrees with run_crew.spine_terminal on the same spine, over one terminal and one non-terminal case), and the archive directory does not already exist. Then it git mv's every top-level entry under .agent-work/<work-id>/ EXCEPT the bound spine and its journal -- names DERIVED from Path(spine_path).name and that name plus '.journal', NEVER the literal strings 'spine.json'/'spine.json.journal', each call naming its own paths; then the spine and its journal LAST; then commits. Never git add -A and never a bare dot. It reports a verdict naming branch, HEAD and 'ready to PR'. It does NOT open a PR and does NOT remove a worktree. Archive name is <YYYY-MM-DD>-<work-id with / replaced by ->, with today passed in as a parameter.

CLOSE CRITERIA:
- close_work called with the lease still active refuses and leaves the work area byte-for-byte untouched
- close_work called with a non-terminal gate refuses and names the offending gate
- close_work called when the archive directory already exists refuses rather than overwriting
- a real spine driven to terminal and released is archived with spine.json LAST -- an interruption after the other entries move leaves spine.json and its journal still at the ORIGINAL path, so a retry finds them
- a source guard over close_work's own body proves no 'git add -A' and no bare '.' reaches a staging call, with a MUTATED copy of the function as the positive control proving the guard can fail
- the archived spine keeps origin and every gate's evidence[] intact
- MANDATORY, and untestable by any matched-pair fixture: close a spine whose basename is NOT what open_work writes (an execute.json) and assert it still moved LAST. Every other fixture closes a spine open_work itself created, so a literal hardcode would pass all of them -- and this Commander's own driving spine is named execute.json (measured: spine.json 48 vs execute.json 40 at depth 3 under .agent-work/; 43 vs 42 excluding the archive -- both conventions are in heavy use)
- the interruption fixture is SIMULATED, and say so: monkeypatch the mover to raise after the non-spine entries move and before the spine-last step, then assert the spine and journal are still at the ORIGINAL path. A real process kill between two git operations is out of scope for this gate

Every guard needs a VIOLATING case and an INNOCENT case in the tests/test_mcp_adoption.py::_cli_only_verb_violations house style -- a test that exercises only the happy path measures the mechanism, not the boundary. Attach the returned IMPLEMENTER_RESULT with --field status=complete.

g3-implement.title: the door — spine_open and spine_close: implement
g3-implement.imperative:
Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md for g3 and dispatch a constellation-implementer crew through scripts/run_crew.py with --parent naming THIS Commander session (never the Admiral) and an explicit --model sonnet. TASK: Add spine_open and spine_close to scripts/mcp_spine_server.py per LIFECYCLE_CONTRACT.md section 6. They are dispatched from call_lifecycle_tool, a NEW MODULE-LEVEL SIBLING of call_tool. call_tool's body is NOT TOUCHED and its choke-point pin stays exactly as strict. spine_open takes work_id/spec/base and never references SPINE, SESSION or run_engine; spine_close takes NO arguments and acts on the bound spine alone. main()'s tools/call branch (line 962) routes every known name to call_tool unconditionally, so main() MUST grow a branch sending the two lifecycle names to call_lifecycle_tool -- route in main(), never inside call_tool. THE TRAP, named at plan time so it is not discovered mid-flight: adding two tools to TOOLS breaks THREE coupled sites in THREE files -- tests/test_mcp_identity.py:998-999 (iterates module.TOOLS, indexes TOOL_MINIMAL_ARGS[tool['name']] -> KeyError); tests/test_mcp_adoption.py:236,246 (set(DOOR_TOOL_NAMES) == server.TOOL_NAMES, and len(...) == 9); tests/test_crew_launcher.py:536,551 (derives the crew grant from TOOL_NAMES, asserts len(...) == 9). The last two are deliberate regression pins that exist BECAUSE the door once grew 7->9 while a hand-typed list froze, so updating them is the required work, not a workaround -- and :536 means the lifecycle tools must also be added to CREW_ALLOWED_TOOLS or a dispatched crew cannot call them. The REQUIRED fix is to scope the identity sweep to the engine tools (TOOL_NAMES minus the lifecycle tool names) and update the two counts and the grant. The FORBIDDEN fix is to handle the new tools inside call_tool to make the sweep pass -- that is the exact regression the pin exists to catch, arriving disguised as test maintenance. Ship the lifecycle surface its OWN containment pin: an AST pin over call_lifecycle_tool with a mutated positive control, and an assertion that spine_open's path never references SPINE/SESSION/run_engine.

CLOSE CRITERIA:
- test_call_tool_can_only_produce_content_two_ways is UNMODIFIED and green
- a new AST pin over call_lifecycle_tool refuses any third return shape, with a mutated positive control
- a check proves spine_open's dispatch path never references SPINE, SESSION or run_engine
- a full stdio JSON-RPC round trip opens a throwaway work id in a tmp git repo and closes it, with the readiness verdict naming branch, commit and 'ready to PR'
- .mcp.json is not modified -- a tool is not a server
- all three coupled sites updated, and tests/test_mcp_adoption.py + tests/test_crew_launcher.py green

Every guard needs a VIOLATING case and an INNOCENT case in the tests/test_mcp_adoption.py::_cli_only_verb_violations house style -- a test that exercises only the happy path measures the mechanism, not the boundary. Attach the returned IMPLEMENTER_RESULT with --field status=complete.
